key_insight: Time-domain EEG autoencoders can learn broad spectral shifts, but standard reconstruction losses tend to under-represent high-frequency information because of 1/f-like power decay.
clinical_relevance: For EEG-based cancer and brain-disorder biomarker pipelines, preserving subtle high-frequency signatures may improve latent features used for early detection and stratification.
method: Compared LSTMVAE, VAEEG, Transformer, and an EEG foundation model for unsupervised representation learning.
Used synthetic experiments to test how spectral content is retained under time-domain reconstruction.
Examined whether larger latent spaces and loss/gradient choices change high-frequency attenuation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both synthetic experiments and empirical validation, showing that autoencoders captured macro-scale changes like alpha slowing but weakened high-frequency components under MSE-based training.
watch_item: Increasing latent dimensionality can reduce attenuation, but it also reduces compactness and may hurt generative stability.
paper_title: Spectral Considerations on Unsupervised Time-domain EEG Representation Learning with Deep Networks
